800 AM HST Sat Aug 22 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lala, located north of the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National
Monument, and on Tropical Storm Moke, located about 450 miles
southeast of Hilo, Hawaii.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Sat Aug 22 2026
 
...HURRICANE LALA CONTINUING NORTHWESTWARD AT A SLOWER FORWARD
SPEED...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...31.0N 172.7W
ABOUT 305 MI...490 KM NE OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 380 MI...615 KM ENE OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...75 MPH...120 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...981 MB...28.97 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Lala was located
near latitude 31.0 North, longitude 172.7 West. Lala is moving
toward the northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h) and this motion is
expected to continue for the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 75 mph (120 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days, 
and Lala's winds could decrease below hurricane force tonight.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles (95 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 255 miles
(405 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 981 mb (28.97 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Large surf associated with Lala will affect western sections
of the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument for the next
couple of days. These large waves could inundate some low-lying
atolls, especially from Maro Reef to Kure Atoll.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Lala Forecast Discussion Number 42
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sat Aug 22 2026 
221 
WTPA42 PHFO 222034
TCDCP2
 
Hurricane Lala Discussion Number  42
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Sat Aug 22 2026

Lala’s convective structure hasn’t changed much over the past 6 h, 
which consists of tightly curved bands.  Only some of the area of 
these convective bands consists of deep convection with cloud tops 
colder than -30C, whereas only moderate convection covers the 
remainder of the convective band area, with cloud top temperatures 
between 0C and -30C.  The latest subjective Dvorak classifications 
are T4.0/65 kt from JTWC and T3.5/55 kt from PHFO.  Since convection 
has been fairly meager for a while now, and we are 12 hours removed 
from the earlier 09Z ASCAT pass mentioned in the discussion from the 
15Z advisory, the initial intensity it again nudged downward, and is 
set at 65 kt for this advisory. 

Lala has slowed down over the past 12 hours, and the initial motion 
is estimated to be northwestward, or 305 degrees at 6 kt.  There is 
no change to the forecast track philosophy. Two mid- to upper-level 
ridges, one to the north and one to the west of Lala will cause the 
cyclone to continue moving slowly northwestward through Monday, 
before it attempts to squeeze in between those two ridges by 
midweek. The northwestward motion in 3-5 days will also be aided by 
an approaching upper-level trough well to the north of the system. 
Only a small change to the right of the previous NHC track forecast 
has been made, and the latest forecast is close to the latest HFIP 
Corrected Consensus (HCCA) model.
 
Relatively dry air and decreasing sea-surface temperatures along 
Lala's track will cause continued weakening.  The shear will 
continue to be weak, and Lala will be moving into an area of colder 
upper-tropospheric temperatures, so those positive factors will be 
enough so that only gradual weakening is expected over the next 
several days.  No major changes are made to the previous NHC 
intensity forecast, which lies near the middle of the guidance 
envelope.  The system is now forecast to lose its convection and 
become post-tropical in about 5 days, as suggested by the GFS and 
ECMWF simulated satellite imageries.

item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sat Aug 22 2026 
601 
WTPA33 PHFO 221433
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Moke Advisory Number   9
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Sat Aug 22 2026
 
...MOKE STRENGTHENS A LITTLE...
...HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS EXPECTED TO BEGIN TONIGHT ON
THE BIG ISLAND OF HAWAII...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.8N 150.2W
ABOUT 470 MI...755 KM SE OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the Hawaiian Islands should closely monitor the
progress of this system.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Moke was
located near latitude 14.8 North, longitude 150.2 West. Moke is
moving toward the west-northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h) and this
general motion is expected during the next several days. On the
forecast track, the center of the storm is expected to pass south of
the Big Island of Hawaii tonight and early Sunday, then well south 
of the smaller main Hawaiian Islands early next week.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Some additional strengthening is expected today, 
but gradual weakening is forecast beginning Sunday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Storm Moke can be found in the Tropical
Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP3 and WMO header
WTPA43 PHFO.
 
WIND: Gusty winds are expected across the Hawaiian Islands tonight 
and Sunday, especially in areas of high terrain.
 
RAINFALL: Moke is expected to produce rainfall totals of 5 to 10
inches with maximum amounts of 15 inches across the Big Island.
Rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches with maximum amounts of 4 inches
are expected on eastern Maui. For the remainder of the islands, 1 to
2 inches of rain are possible. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides for the windward and
southeast Big Island, especially in steep terrain and over areas
that were affected recently by Lala.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Moke,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp3.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by the storm are expected to affect exposed
east and south facing shores of the Hawaiian Islands during the 
next few days. These swells may cause life-threatening surf and rip 
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather 
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Moke Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sat Aug 22 2026 
000
WTPA43 PHFO 221433
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Storm Moke Discussion Number   9
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Sat Aug 22 2026
 
Moke is gaining some strength this morning with deep convection 
increasing in intensity and extent. The Air Force Hurricane Hunters 
have departed the storm, but during their last pass through the 
center they measured a minimum pressure of 994 mb and maximum 850 mb 
flight-level winds of 53 kt. These data support increasing the 
initial wind speed to 45 kt for this advisory. This intensity 
estimate is also in agreement with the latest JTWC Dvorak 
classification and objective estimates from UW-CIMSS. The aircraft 
data and last night's ASCAT pass also showed that the 
tropical-storm-force wind radii are a little larger on the north 
side of the system while the radius of maximum wind has contracted. 
Nonetheless, Moke remains a compact tropical storm. The NOAA and Air 
Force Hurricane Hunters are scheduled to investigate the system 
again later today.

The tropical storm is moving a little faster to the west-northwest, 
or 290/10 kt. This general motion is expected to persist during the 
next several days as a low- to mid-level ridge strengthens to the 
north of the storm. This track should bring the center of Moke 
roughly a couple of hundred miles to the south of the Big Island 
late tonight and early Sunday and then well south of the smaller 
main Hawaiian Islands after that. Since Moke is expected to remain 
compact, and because there is high confidence in the short term 
track forecast, no tropical storm watches or warnings appear to be 
necessary for Hawaii. However, the storm is expected to be close 
enough to produce gusty winds in portions of the Hawaiian Islands, 
especially in areas of high terrain, late tonight through early next 
week. In addition, most of the associated moisture is expected to be 
on the north side of the cyclone, so areas of heavy rain are 
forecast there during the next few days. 
 
Moke will likely strengthen a little more today while it remains in 
generally conducive environmental conditions. However, the 
combination of dry air entrainment and an increase in vertical wind 
shear should cause the storm to gradually lose strength beginning 
Sunday and continuing into next week. The intensity models are in 
good agreement, and little change was made to the previous NHC 
forecast. In fact, most of the models show Moke dissipating toward 
the end of the forecast period.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Moke will begin to 
impact the Big Island of Hawaii late tonight, with rain spreading 
westward across the remainder of the Hawaiian Islands Sunday into 
Monday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and 
mudslides for the windward and southeast Big Island, especially in 
steep terrain and over areas that were affected recently by Lala. 
 
2. Although the strongest winds associated with Moke are expected to
pass south of the Hawaiian Islands, strong gusty winds are likely,
particularly in areas within and downslope of higher terrain.
 
3. Swells generated by the storm may cause life-threatening surf
and rip current conditions through early next week for exposed east
and south facing shores of the Hawaiian Islands.
